categories.name: Computer Science
categories.description: Programs in software, algorithms, and computing systems, from research-oriented computer science degrees to applied programming diplomas.

tips.title: Build personal projects
tips.detail: Ship real software — apps, games, tools — and keep the code in a public GitHub portfolio. Concrete projects are the strongest evidence of genuine interest in computing.

tips.title: Write the CCC and Euclid contests
tips.detail: The Canadian Computing Competition and the Euclid math contest are recognized by admissions committees across Ontario and give a measurable signal beyond course grades.

tips.title: Join hackathons
tips.detail: Weekend hackathons (many are free for high-school students) produce portfolio pieces, teamwork stories, and connections you can point to in supplementary applications.

categories.name: Nursing
categories.description: Degree and collaborative programs preparing students to become registered nurses in hospital, community, and long-term-care settings.

tips.title: Volunteer in a hospital or long-term-care home
tips.detail: Sustained volunteering in patient-facing settings shows you understand the realities of care work and gives you concrete experiences to draw on in tests like CASPer.

tips.title: Get First Aid and CPR certified
tips.detail: Standard First Aid with CPR-C is inexpensive, widely available, and demonstrates early commitment to health care; many clinical placements will require it anyway.

categories.name: Business & Commerce
categories.description: Commerce, management, and business administration programs covering accounting, finance, marketing, and entrepreneurship.

tips.title: Compete in DECA
tips.detail: DECA case competitions build the presentation and analysis skills business programs screen for, and placing at provincials is a strong line on any supplementary application.

tips.title: Hold a part-time job or start a small venture
tips.detail: Real work experience — a retail job, tutoring business, or online shop — is concrete proof of initiative and is exactly what commerce supplemental essays ask about.

tips.title: Take on a leadership role
tips.detail: Student council, club treasurer, or event organizing shows you can lead and manage people and budgets, which business admissions value highly.

categories.name: Engineering
categories.description: Accredited engineering programs spanning mechanical, electrical, civil, mechatronics, and computer disciplines.

tips.title: Join a FIRST Robotics team
tips.detail: FIRST Robotics is the most widely recognized pre-engineering activity in Ontario; design, build, and competition roles all translate directly into engineering application answers.

tips.title: Enter a science fair
tips.detail: A well-documented science fair project shows you can define a problem, iterate on a design, and present results — the core loop of engineering work.

tips.title: Write math and physics contests
tips.detail: Contests like Euclid, CSMC, and the Sir Isaac Newton (SIN) physics exam give admissions a standardized signal of problem-solving strength beyond your course marks.

categories.name: Health & Life Sciences
categories.description: Life science, health science, and medical science programs that commonly lead to medicine, research, and other health professions.

tips.title: Volunteer in research or clinical settings
tips.detail: Helping in a university lab, hospital unit, or community clinic shows sustained commitment to health care and produces the specific stories supplementary applications reward.

tips.title: Present a science fair project
tips.detail: An independent research project — especially one with a health or biology focus — demonstrates scientific thinking beyond the classroom.

tips.title: OUAC application deadline
tips.detail: Apply through OUAC by January 15, 2027 — the equal-consideration date for Fall 2027 entry to Ontario universities.

tips.title: President's/entrance scholar consideration
tips.detail: Admitted students with averages of roughly 92% and above are automatically considered for University of Toronto entrance scholarships, including President's Scholars awards.

supplementary.name: Rotman Supplemental Application
supplementary.description: Timed video interview plus written responses, completed after applying.

tips.title: Prepare for the Rotman Supplemental
tips.detail: The video interview and written responses are weighted alongside your marks. Practice answering on camera within a time limit and have specific stories ready about leadership and initiative.

programs.name: Computer Science
programs.notes: Admission averages of successful applicants are typically well above the published minimum; the AIF and contest results matter for borderline candidates.

supplementary.name: Admission Information Form (AIF)
supplementary.description: Waterloo's supplementary form covering activities, interests, and circumstances; scored and factored into admission decisions.

tips.title: Make the AIF count
tips.detail: The Admission Information Form can meaningfully boost a borderline average. Be specific: name your projects, contests, and roles rather than describing interests in general terms.

tips.title: Write the Canadian Computing Competition
tips.detail: A strong CCC score is concrete evidence of programming ability and one of the clearest ways to strengthen your AIF for Waterloo CS.

tips.title: OUAC application deadline
tips.detail: Apply through OUAC by January 15, 2027 — the equal-consideration date for Fall 2027 entry to Ontario universities.

tips.title: President's Scholarship of Distinction
tips.detail: Automatic consideration by admission average: 95%+ earns the President's Scholarship of Distinction, 90–94.9% the President's Scholarship, and 85–89.9% the Merit Scholarship.

programs.name: Software Engineering
programs.notes: One of the most competitive programs in Canada; successful applicants typically present averages in the high 90s along with demonstrated programming experience.

supplementary.name: Admission Information Form (AIF)
supplementary.description: Waterloo's supplementary form; for Software Engineering it includes demonstrated programming experience, which is expected of competitive applicants.

tips.title: Show programming experience on the AIF
tips.detail: Software Engineering expects demonstrated programming experience. Use the AIF to point at shipped projects, repositories, and contest results — vague enthusiasm does not score.

tips.title: Write the Canadian Computing Competition
tips.detail: A strong CCC score is concrete evidence of programming ability and one of the clearest ways to strengthen your AIF for Software Engineering.

programs.notes: Grades act as a threshold; above the cutoff, selection is driven primarily by the supplementary application.

supplementary.name: BHSc Supplementary Application
supplementary.description: Short written responses reviewed by multiple assessors; the dominant selection factor above the grade cutoff.

tips.title: Invest heavily in the supplementary application
tips.detail: Above the grade cutoff, the BHSc supplementary application outweighs marks. Draft your responses early, get feedback, and answer the questions actually asked rather than reciting achievements.
